configuration.load_balance_note: Uniform spatial particle initialization across z assigns approximately N_p / size particles to each equal-height slab and represents the best-case scenario for parallel load balance.
configuration.profiled_stage_note: Per-stage breakdown timings are measured in a separate profiled pass (ps.profile=True, solver._profile_mpi=True). Per-stage cudaStreamSynchronize() barriers inflate stage times relative to the unprofiled coupled step median, and for MPI runs (size > 1) each stage is reduced as the maximum over ranks (MPI.MAX) and then summed across stages (sum_s max_r t_{r,s} >= max_r sum_s t_{r,s}), which is why the 2-GPU stage sum can exceed the profiled step total.
configuration.baseline_and_efficiency_note: The library default is periodic cell sorting sort_every=50; headline 2-GPU speedup (b) compares 2 L4 NCCL against 1 L4 with sort_every=50 (pre-sorted after warm-up and timed over >= sort_every steps per repeat so amortised sort cost is included). Speedup (a) compares unsorted runs (sort_every=0). Parallel efficiency (c) is defined against the equal-work 1-L4 half-domain N_p/2 control (t_half_ctrl / t_2gpu), isolating communication and migration overhead from single-GPU domain-size effects; apparent efficiency against the full-domain 1-L4 baseline ((t_1gpu / t_2gpu) / 2) is reported separately.

caption: At N_p = 10,000,000, the headline 2-GPU NCCL speedup at the library default (periodic cell sorting sort_every=50, amortised sort cost included) is (b) 1.8x (sorted push+deposit 5.1 vs 5.1 ns/particle; sort call 21 ms / 1% amortised share on 1 L4 and 10 ms / 1% on 2 L4), compared with (a) 2.0x with NCCL and 2.0x with pinned-host MPI against the unsorted 1-L4 baseline (sort_every=0), and (c) parallel efficiency vs the equal-work 1-L4 64x64x64 N_p/2 half-domain control (t_half_ctrl / t_2gpu) is 87% (whereas apparent efficiency (t_1gpu / t_2gpu) / 2 against the full-domain unsorted 1-L4 baseline is 100%). At N_p = 10,000,000, unsorted per-particle push+deposit changes by -11% on 2 GPUs (5.5 vs 6.1 ns/particle on 1 L4) and by -14% (5.3 ns/particle) on the 1-L4 64x64x64 N_p/2 half-domain control. In the 1-L4 fixed-density working-set sweep (nz = 16..256, push+deposit kernel working set 5.0..75.8 MB and total field+current working set 15.0..227.4 MB vs 50.3 MB L2 cache), unsorted push+deposit starts at 5.4 ns/particle (nz=16, push+deposit kernel working set 5.0 MB, total field+current working set 15.0 MB) and rises to 8.5 ns/particle (nz=256, push+deposit kernel working set 75.8 MB, total field+current working set 227.4 MB): the rise is gradual, beginning in the push+deposit kernel working-set interval 19.2..28.6 MB (nz=64..96, total field+current working set 57.5..85.8 MB), and no discrete step at the 50.3 MB L2 cache size is resolved under the criterion requiring the L2-bracketing jump to exceed both k=3.0 times the independent-duplicate noise (0.14 ns/particle, threshold 0.41 ns/particle) and the jumps implied by the two neighbouring intervals' slopes per log working set (across the L2-bracketing push+deposit kernel working-set interval 38.0..56.9 MB the jump is 0.82 ns/particle vs 0.73 ns/particle from lower neighbour, 1.9 ns/particle from upper neighbour implied by neighbour log-slopes; across the L2-bracketing total field+current working-set interval 43.4..57.5 MB the change is -0.17 ns/particle). By contrast, the cell-sorted curve (sort_every=50) is flat within duplicate noise over the rising regime (5.1-5.5 ns/particle across push+deposit kernel working set 19.2..75.8 MB and total field+current working set 57.5..227.4 MB; 4.6-5.5 ns/particle over the full sweep), demonstrating that the unsorted penalty is locality-dependent and consistent with an L2 cache-residency effect as a stated hypothesis. Two-GPU execution pays 15% of the profiled stage sum (17% of the unprofiled step median) in particle migration and compaction. In the separate profiled pass, each stage time is reduced as the maximum over MPI ranks and then summed across stages, which is why the 2-GPU stage sum can exceed the profiled step total. All 16 sorted controls passed the unsorted-referenced profiling consistency check (|t_prof_s - t_med_s| <= |t_prof_u - t_med_u| + jitter_u). Electromagnetic FIT field updates (B + E advance) are ~2% of the step at N_p = 10,000,000 (<= 17% across N_p >= 10^6), so the field solver's own scaling is not tested in the particle-dominated regime. At N_p = 100,000 (field- and communication-latency-bound), the 2-GPU speedups vs unsorted 1 L4 are 1.5x with NCCL and 1.1x with pinned-host MPI. Run-to-run variation between independent cloud VMs is several percent, and quoted values are from a single run unless a two-run min-max range is shown. Comparing 2 GPUs against 1 GPU on a single node measures a 2-GPU speedup, not a multi-rank strong-scaling curve.
